intro.text:
Airing a room in winter: is a wide-open window really better than a tilted one?

Same room, same cold day. Only the window differs.

captions.text: Colours show air temperature: blue is cold, red is warm. Watch the window.
Wide open: heavy cold air pours in along the floor while warm air escapes above it.
Tilted: cold air sinks into the pocket behind the pane, and the exchange almost stops.
The radiator keeps the tilted room warm, but it is heating the same old air.
The wide-open room cools quickly because most of its air is being replaced.
The counters show how much of each room's air now comes from outside.

intro.text:
How much of the stale room air actually gets replaced?

We tagged all of the room's air and watched where it goes.

captions.text: Red is the room's original air. Blue is fresh air from outside.
Wide open: fresh air floods in low and pushes the old air out at the top.
Tilted: very little gets past the pane, so the room keeps its old air.
The radiator's warm plume stirs the air, but stirring is not replacing.
Mixing spreads the fresh air through the whole wide-open room.
